planting.note: Direct sow or set out transplants after the last frost in warm soil, providing a trellis to keep fruit straight; Picolino is a parthenocarpic mini cucumber bred to set seedless fruit without pollination.

directions: Direct sow after danger of frost has passed, training vines onto a trellis or cage for straighter, cleaner fruit. Picolino is a parthenocarpic mini cucumber, meaning it reliably sets thin-skinned, seedless, 3-4 inch fruit without needing pollinator activity, making it dependable even in low-bee conditions or under row cover. The skin is tender enough to eat without peeling and the flavor is mild and non-bitter, making it a popular choice for lunchbox snacking and pickling whole. Because fruit sizes up quickly, plants need picking every day or two at peak season to prevent cucumbers from overgrowing and to keep the vine setting new fruit.

common_name: Burpless Beauty Cucumber (Mild Non-Bitter Slicing Cucumber)

planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed; Burpless Beauty is a classic slicing cucumber selected for thin, dark-green skin and a mild flavor with little of the bitterness or gas-causing compounds found in older slicing types.

directions: Direct sow seeds an inch deep into warm, well-drained soil in full sun, and provide a trellis to keep fruit straight and reduce disease pressure. Burpless Beauty produces long, slender, dark-green fruit with thin, tender skin that can be eaten unpeeled, and it was bred specifically to be milder and easier to digest than standard slicing cucumbers, a trait long marketed as burpless. Vines are vigorous and productive over a long summer harvest window when picked regularly. Harvest fruit at 8-10 inches while still glossy and firm; letting cucumbers oversize on the vine slows further production and can make the skin tougher and more bitter.
sources: Burpee — Burpless Beauty Cucumber variety description

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant 2-4 weeks before the last frost for a spring crop, and again in late summer for fall harvest; Sandy is a compact oakleaf lettuce, the first AAS lettuce winner since 1985, bred for slow bolting and strong powdery mildew resistance.

directions: Direct sow in early spring or late summer, thinning to about 8-10 inches apart since Sandy forms a compact, uniformly mounded loose head rather than a large sprawling plant. Named an All-America Selections winner as the first lettuce to earn the award since 1985, Sandy is an oakleaf type with a multitude of sweet, frilly, dark green lobed leaves, notable disease resistance (especially to powdery mildew), and a strong tolerance for heat and heat-stress bitterness that lets it hold quality well past when older lettuces would bolt. Its compact 10-12 inch mounded habit fits neatly into a flowerpot, raised bed, or tight garden row. Harvest by cutting whole loose heads at maturity, or pick outer leaves cut-and-come-again style for baby leaf salads in as little as 30 days.
